title: VSp 6 sweet potato (Super Bureau): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: VSp 6 sweet potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: VSp 6 sweet potato is a sweet potato variety. 110 to 115 days to harvest, 22.4 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: VSp 6 is a registered sweet potato variety, also sold or known as Super Bureau. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1988. It comes from ViSCA (now VSU). It takes 110 to 115 days from planting to harvest, with 22.37 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

**Yield:** 22.37 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about VSp 6 sweet potato
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

VSp 6 sweet potato takes 110 to 115 days from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 26 sweet potato varieties with a day count, 114.5 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 22.37 t/ha beats the average of its group, 15.15. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives 110 to 115 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit sweet potato fields most often: [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Yellow orange flesh with vitamin A.
**Uses:** Feed, starch, sweetpotato powder, sold fresh in Central Luzon markets.
Registered in 1988 with the Philippine Seed Board.
One of only five of 48 clones found tolerant to viruses in Central Luzon tests.
Registry notes high moisture, recommended for feed and starch rather than table use.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: widely adopted by Central Luzon farmers and the market benchmark other kamote varieties are compared against there, grown on the large Moncada, Tarlac cooperative farm. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant VSp 6 sweet potato
Pick by use and market: yellow or orange flesh for snacks and fries, purple for processing, white for boiling. Weevils are the main enemy, so plant clean cuttings and harvest on time.

items.q: Is Super Bureau the same as VSp 6?
items.a: Yes. Super Bureau is another name for VSp 6. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 110 to 115 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 22.37 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of VSp 6?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
